Build a Network

Source: R/build_network.R, R/summary_network.R
build_network.Rd

build_network() estimates a network from sequences, an event log, one-hot codes or numeric variables, and returns a netobject: the object every other Nestimate verb reads (bootstrap, permutation, centrality, clustering, plotting). One call covers two kinds of network. Transition networks ("relative", "frequency", "co_occurrence" and their variants) are directed or undirected graphs of states, where an edge says how often or how likely one state follows another. Association networks ("cor", "pcor", "glasso", "ising", "mgm") are undirected graphs of variables, where an edge is a correlation or a (regularised) partial correlation. The Estimators section lists every method and its aliases; estimators added with register_estimator() are called the same way.

Column roles are declared, never read from names or values. An event log needs action, and usually actor, time or session; a wide table needs position columns named as a numbered run (T1, T2, ...) or listed in state_cols; one-hot data needs codes or format = "onehot". Input that fits none of these raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input instead of being read one way or another.

The weights are point estimates. Before reading single edges, see how far they move under resampling with bootstrap_network(), and compare groups with permutation() rather than by eye. An event log that yields a single sequence is reported with a message of class nestimate_single_sequence: that network describes one sequence and cannot be resampled.

Usage

build_network(
  data,
  method,
  actor = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  session = NULL,
  order = NULL,
  codes = NULL,
  group = NULL,
  format = "auto",
  window_size = 3L,
  mode = c("non-overlapping", "overlapping"),
  scaling = NULL,
  threshold = 0,
  level = NULL,
  time_threshold = 900,
  timezone = "UTC",
  predictability = TRUE,
  state_cols = NULL,
  metadata_cols = NULL,
  start = FALSE,
  end = FALSE,
  params = list(),
  labels = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'netobject'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject_group'
print(x, digits = 3L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject_ml'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'netobject_group'
summary(object, combined = TRUE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.netobject'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.netobject_group'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

data

The data to estimate from: a data frame of sequences (one row per sequence, one column per position), an event log (one row per event, with action set), one-hot code columns, numeric variables (one row per observation) for the association methods, or a square symmetric correlation or covariance matrix. A fitted net_clustering or net_mmm object also works: its per-cluster networks are built, with the scaling, threshold, start, end and params given here, and returned as a netobject_group. The relative networks of a net_mmm are the fitted chains: scaling and threshold are applied to them, and any other argument raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

method

The estimator: a built-in method or alias (see the Estimators section), or a name added with register_estimator(); list_estimators() lists them. Required, except when data is a net_clustering or net_mmm object, whose own method is used.

actor

The column naming who each row belongs to (a person, a team). In an event log, each actor's events form a sequence, split further by session or time_threshold. With level, it is the id the multilevel decomposition groups by. Default NULL.

action

The column holding each event's state; setting it declares the data an event log. Column names give no role: action, actor, time and session are read only when set. A column called Action with nothing declared raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, and an undeclared time or session column beside action is named in a message of class nestimate_column_role. Default NULL.

time

The timestamp column of an event log. Events are ordered by it, and a gap longer than time_threshold starts a new sequence. Default NULL.

session

The column identifying sessions in an event log; each session is its own sequence, also without actor. Default NULL.

order

The column that orders events sharing a timestamp; without it, those events keep their row order. Default NULL.

codes

The one-hot code columns (one per state, 1 when the state is active); setting them declares one-hot data. Default NULL.

group

A column to split the data by: one network is estimated per value and the result is a netobject_group. Default NULL.

format

How to read data. "auto" (default) reads an event log when action is set, one-hot data when codes is set, and wide positions otherwise; it never infers one-hot data from the values. "wide", "long" and "onehot" force a reading. The association methods and the wtna methods read 0/1 columns as they always do.

window_size

For one-hot data: how many consecutive rows form one window (default 3). Windows on sequence data are set through params instead.

mode

For one-hot data: "non-overlapping" (default) or "overlapping" windows; wtna() describes how overlapping windows are counted. Wide and long sequence data ignore it.

scaling

Rescaling applied to the weights after estimation, in the order given: "minmax" maps the non-zero weights into (0, 1], "max" divides by the largest absolute weight, "rank" replaces the non-zero weights by their ranks, and "normalize" makes each row's absolute weights sum to 1. Zero weights stay zero under every option. Combine them as in c("rank", "minmax"). Default NULL (none).

threshold

Weights whose absolute value is below this are set to zero. Default 0 (none). For method = "mgm", "LW" or "none" instead selects mgm's coefficient-thresholding rule (a threshold in params takes precedence); any other non-numeric value raises an error.

level

Multilevel decomposition for the undirected association methods (cor, pcor, glasso, mgm): "between" estimates the network of person means, "within" the network of deviations from them, and "both" returns the two as a netobject_ml. It needs an id column, given as actor or as params$id; a directed method raises an error. Default NULL (no decomposition). For method = "mgm", a numeric vector instead gives one category count per modelled variable (1 for continuous ones), after group, actor and metadata columns are set aside; it is checked and kept for compatibility, and the fit reads the categories from the data.

time_threshold

The longest gap, in seconds, between two events of the same sequence in an event log; a longer gap starts a new sequence. FALSE turns the split off, so each actor (or actor-session) is one sequence. Default 900.

timezone

The Olson time zone for timestamps without an offset (passed to prepare()); timestamps with an offset, such as ...Z or +02:00, are converted from it. Default "UTC".

predictability

Whether to compute each node's predictability (the R-squared of the node on its neighbours) for the undirected association methods cor, pcor and glasso. It is stored on the network, and cograph::splot() draws it as a ring around each node. Default TRUE.

state_cols

The columns of a wide table that are sequence positions; every other column of the cleaned input goes to the network's metadata. Declared columns are positions even when they hold only 0 and 1; one-hot data is declared with codes or format = "onehot". With nothing declared, the frame must be one column or hold position columns named as a numbered run (a shared prefix and a number, T1, T2, ..., or 1, 2, ...); numeric columns beside the run and character or factor columns outside it are then covariates. Any other frame on a sequence method, and columns of only 0 and 1, raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input: nothing says whether they are positions or one-hot codes. Default NULL.

metadata_cols

Columns to keep as the network's metadata (covariates), never as positions; they cannot overlap state_cols. A column left out of a numbered run of positions is named in a message of class nestimate_column_role, and listing it here or in state_cols settles it. Default NULL.

start

A start state put before every sequence, so the network shows where sequences begin (an edge from it to each sequence's first state). FALSE (default) adds none, TRUE adds one labelled "Start", and a single string adds one with that label. Only for the transition methods relative, frequency, co_occurrence, attention, ngram, gap and reverse; any other method, wtna included, raises an error.

end

An end state put in the cell after each sequence's last observed state, so the network shows where sequences stop. It has no outgoing edges and no self-loop, unlike mark_terminal_state(), which fills all trailing missing cells with an absorbing state. FALSE (default) adds none, TRUE adds one labelled "End", and a single string adds one with that label. Same methods as start.

params

Settings passed to the estimator, as a named list, such as list(gamma = 0.5) for glasso or list(n_gram = 3) for ngram. The list is stored on the network, so bootstrap_network() and the other resampling verbs re-estimate with exactly the same settings. The transition methods take tna's sequence options weighted and concat, and the low-level begin_state / end_state that start and end set. window_size (with window_span, or windowed = TRUE for a size of 2) counts relative, frequency and co_occurrence between consecutive non-overlapping blocks of that many positions, as tna::tna() does; other transition methods raise an error of class nestimate_bad_input, and mode = "overlapping" a warning of class nestimate_ignored_mode. Column roles given here (action, id, id_col, actor, time, session, order, cols, codes, group) must name existing columns, and must agree with the same role given directly.

labels

New display labels for the nodes, applied after estimation: a two-column data frame (name, label), a named character vector c(name = "label") or a named list. It rewrites the node labels and the weight matrix's dimnames; nodes not listed keep their names.

...

Further arguments for the estimator. For event logs, prepare()'s time options unix_time_unit, is_unix_time and custom_format go to prepare() instead (e.g. unix_time_unit = "milliseconds"). For the print() and summary() methods: ignored.

x

For the print() methods: a netobject, netobject_group or netobject_ml, or the result of summary() on one.

digits

For print() of a netobject_group: decimal places of the weight range. Default 3.

object

For summary(): a netobject or netobject_group.

combined

For summary() of a netobject_group: TRUE (default) joins the groups' metrics into one data frame with a column per group; FALSE returns a named list of the per-group tables.

Value

A netobject (class c("netobject", "cograph_network")). Print it for an overview; extract_edges() gives one row per edge, extract_transition_matrix() and extract_initial_probs() the weights and initial-state probabilities, and cograph::splot() draws it. summary() returns the descriptive metrics, one row per metric (a netobject_group gives one column per group). The print() methods return their input invisibly. The netobject's fields:

data

The state columns of the cleaned input data, as a data frame.

metadata

Data frame of the non-state columns of the cleaned input (and, for long input, the per-sequence metadata), or NULL.

weights

The estimated network weight matrix.

nodes

Data frame with columns id, label, name, x, y.

edges

Data frame of non-zero edges with integer from/to (node IDs) and numeric weight.

directed

Logical. Whether the network is directed.

method

The resolved method name.

params

The params list used (for reproducibility).

scaling

The scaling applied (or NULL).

threshold

The threshold applied.

n_nodes

Number of nodes.

n_edges

Number of non-zero edges.

level

Decomposition level used, or NULL; for mgm, the category count of each variable.

build_args

The resolved column/format arguments (actor, action, time, session, order, codes, format, window_size, mode) used for this build.

meta

List with source, layout, and tna metadata (cograph-compatible).

node_groups

Node groupings data frame, or NULL.

predictability

Named numeric vector of R-squared predictability values per node, for cor, pcor and glasso when predictability = TRUE; NULL otherwise.

The estimator's own results are kept beside these fields, depending on the method: for example frequency_matrix and initial for relative, frequency, ngram, gap and reverse (only initial for attention, neither for co_occurrence), cor_matrix and the sample size n for cor, pcor and glasso, precision_matrix for pcor and glasso, and lambda_selected for glasso.

With level = "both", the result is a netobject_ml holding the between-person and within-person networks (between and within, each a netobject) and the method. level = "between" or "within" returns a single netobject estimated on the decomposed data.

With group, or when data is a net_clustering or net_mmm object, the result is a netobject_group: a named list of netobjects, one per group, that records the grouping column in its group_col attribute.

Details

build_network() resolves the method alias, checks the declared column arguments before the format is resolved, and takes the estimator from the registry. For an association method with level, it first decomposes the data into person means ("between") or deviations from them ("within"). It then calls the estimator with data and params, applies scaling and then threshold to the weight matrix, and extracts the edges.

In an event log, action alone makes all rows one sequence in row order; session, or a time gap above time_threshold, splits them without an actor. When the log yields a single sequence, a message of class nestimate_single_sequence says so, because such a network cannot be validated by bootstrap or the other confirmatory tests.

For method = "mgm", missing continuous values are filled with the observed column mean and missing categorical values with the modal level. This keeps the rows and is psychnets' documented na_method = "pairwise" policy; it is not pairwise deletion.

For a network with non-negative weights, the summary() values equal those of tna::summary.tna() from tna 1.5.4 on.

Estimators

"relative"

Transition probabilities (row-normalised counts); directed. Aliases: "tna", "transition".

"frequency"

Transition counts; directed. Aliases: "ftna", "counts".

"co_occurrence"

Co-occurrence within sequences; undirected. Aliases: "cna", "wcna", "co-occurrence".

"attention"

Decay-weighted transitions; directed. Alias: "atna".

"ngram"

Adjacent pairs counted once per n-gram window; directed. Aliases: "n-gram", "n_gram".

"gap"

Pairs up to max_gap + 1 positions apart, weighted 1 / distance; directed.

"reverse"

Reply network, the transpose of "frequency"; directed.

"wtna"

Window-based transitions on one-hot data; directed. Alias: "wtna_transition".

"wtna_cooccurrence"

Window-based co-occurrence on one-hot data; undirected.

"cor"

Pearson correlations; undirected. Aliases: "corr", "correlation".

"pcor"

Partial correlations, unregularised; undirected. Alias: "partial".

"glasso"

EBIC graphical lasso partial correlations; undirected. Aliases: "ebicglasso", "regularized".

"ising"

Ising model (L1-penalised logistic regression); undirected. Alias: "isingfit".

"mgm"

Mixed graphical model; undirected. Aliases: "mixed", "mixed_graphical".

"ngram", "gap" and "reverse" are tna::build_model()'s types "n-gram", "gap" and "reverse". Their settings go in params: list(n_gram = 2), list(max_gap = 1) and list(weighted = FALSE) are the defaults. All three return raw weights; add scaling = "normalize" for row probabilities.

Methods

Printing a netobject shows the kind of network, the range of its weights (with the numbers of positive and negative edges for cor, pcor, glasso and ising, the mean weight otherwise), the weight matrix under the node labels, the initial probabilities and the predictability values when present, the sample size for cor, pcor, glasso and ising, the tuning values of glasso and ising, and any scaling or threshold. Printing a netobject_group gives a header naming its source (a clustering from build_network() on a net_clustering or net_mmm fit, or cluster_network(), or a plain split by the grouping column) and one row per group with its node and edge counts and weight range; when the groups are clusters, it also shows the number and share of sequences in each, in the layout of the build_clusters() and build_mmm() prints. A netobject_ml prints the node, edge and sample counts of its between- and within-person networks.

summary() gives the descriptive metrics tna::summary.tna() reports: node and edge counts, density, mean shortest-path distance, the mean and SD of out- and in-strength, the mean and SD of out-degree, out- and in-degree centralisation (Freeman) and reciprocity. A self-loop counts as an edge, an undirected edge is counted once, and density is capped at 1. Strengths sum absolute weights. Distances take each edge's absolute weight as its length, not its inverse, and pairs with no path between them are left out of the mean. Degree centralisation ignores self-loops, and reciprocity is the share of off-diagonal edges whose reverse is also present (1 for an undirected network). Mean distance and reciprocity are NaN when no pair qualifies. Printing a summary shows the counts as integers and the other metrics to four significant digits.

Examples

seqs <- data.frame(V1 = c("A","B","C","A"), V2 = c("B","C","A","B"))
net <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative")
net
#> Transition Network (relative probabilities) [directed]
#>   Weights: [1.000, 1.000]  |  mean: 1.000
#> 
#>   Weight matrix:
#>     A B C
#>   A 0 1 0
#>   B 0 0 1
#>   C 1 0 0 
#> 
#>   Initial probabilities:
#>   A             0.500  ████████████████████████████████████████
#>   B             0.250  ████████████████████
#>   C             0.250  ████████████████████
# \donttest{
# Transition network (relative probabilities)
seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 30, TRUE), V2 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 30, TRUE),
  V3 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 30, TRUE), V4 = sample(LETTERS[1:4], 30, TRUE)
)
net <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative")
print(net)
#> Transition Network (relative probabilities) [directed]
#>   Weights: [0.143, 0.429]  |  mean: 0.250
#> 
#>   Weight matrix:
#>         A     B     C     D
#>   A 0.310 0.310 0.172 0.207
#>   B 0.353 0.176 0.176 0.294
#>   C 0.261 0.174 0.217 0.348
#>   D 0.429 0.238 0.143 0.190 
#> 
#>   Initial probabilities:
#>   C             0.367  ████████████████████████████████████████
#>   A             0.300  █████████████████████████████████
#>   D             0.233  █████████████████████████
#>   B             0.100  ███████████

# Association network (glasso)
freq_data <- convert_sequence_format(seqs, format = "frequency")
net_glasso <- build_network(freq_data, method = "glasso",
                             params = list(gamma = 0.5, nlambda = 50))

# With scaling
net_scaled <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative",
                             scaling = c("rank", "minmax"))
# }
